title: Bicentralizers of type III₁ factors
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Bicentralizers of type III₁ factors and Connes' bicentralizer problem. Connes–Størmer transitivity makes the asymptotic centralizer of every faithful normal state a II₁ factor; the bicentralizer, its description in the Ocneanu ultrapower, its state-preserving expectation and the Houdayer–Isono self-bicentralizing property; Connes' isomorphism and the bicentralizer flow, built in a single ultrapower; modular averaging, bounded recovery and spectral intertwining rigidity (OpenAI, 2026), which make the flow trivial; Haagerup's criterion for a trivial bicentralizer; Marrakchi's strongly invariant states; and the theorem that every type III₁ factor with separable predual has trivial bicentralizer.
prerequisites: type-iii-factors lesson ultraproducts-and-the-asymptotic-centralizer (Section 1, Lemmas 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, Theorem 5.1, Theorem 6.6, results (B1)-(B8))
OA-MOD lesson OA-MOD-ME (conditional expectations from modular invariance, ME-01, ME-08)
OA-FLOW lesson OA-FLOW-CR (standard-form corners CR-1, CR-3, CR-8; cone vectors CR-4; inequality CR18 of CR-6)
OA-MOD lesson OA-MOD-NC (joint left/right spectral measure NC-20; estimate NC.4)
OA-MOD lessons OA-MOD-FS (FS.1, FS.2), OA-MOD-SF (SF-05), OA-MOD-SK (spectral calculus with domains)
OA-FLOW lessons OA-FLOW-CS (CS3, CS-4), OA-FLOW-MG (MG6, MG9, MG10, MG-5), OA-FLOW-MT (MT25)

checks.exact_checks: numpy (scratch bic_checks.py, 8 Oct 2026): the four estimates of the partial-isometry lemma (first lesson, Lemma 2.2) on 400 random finite-dimensional instances with eps = ||u chi1 u* - chi2|| < 1; the predual estimate ||phi w - e^s w phi|| <= (1 + e^{s/2}) ||(Delta^{1/2} - e^{s/2}) w xi|| on 300 random matrix instances; the Steinhaus fourth-moment identity, exactly by root-of-unity averaging; the scalar inequalities (1-t)^2 <= 1-t^2, |t - 1_[1/2,1](t)| <= 2(t-t^2), (r-K)_+^2 <= r^4/K^2; numpy (scratch bic2_checks.py, 8 Oct 2026): the scalar inequalities (t-s)^2/2 <= |t|t|-s|s|| <= |t-s|(|s|+|t|) on 200000 samples; the joint-spectral integral bounds of Haagerup's criterion lesson, Lemma 3.1, and the layer-cake identity on 200 random matrix instances; the constants of Lemmas 2.1, 2.2 and 4.2 there; the Powers-Stormer inequality for density matrices on 300 instances; the 2x2 predual and vector identities of Lemma 2.1 of the last lesson and the unitary inequality (2.1) on 300 instances; the adjoint relation used in Proposition 3.3 there; the constant bookkeeping of Lemma 4.1 there

open_obligations: The relative bicentralizer theorem (OpenAI, expected amenable subalgebras preserving core commutants): proved for bottom factors of type III_1 in the course relative-bicentralizers-and-core-commutants (lesson an-injective-subalgebra-with-the-same-core-commutant, Theorem 5.2); bottom algebras of other types and with arbitrary centre are recorded as open obligations there.

Consequence of the trivial bicentralizer that this course does not prove: maximal abelian subalgebras with expectation (Houdayer-Isono, Corollary 3.6). Not yet written. The other consequence, Haagerup 1987, Theorem 3.1 (density of faithful normal states with irreducible centralizer), is proved in the course relative-bicentralizers-and-core-commutants, lesson an-injective-subalgebra-with-the-same-core-commutant, Corollary 5.3.
